answer: An agent economy dispatching tugboats between a river terminal and a busy harbor can resist Sybil attacks using proof-of-burn. Every new agent must permanently destroy native tokens by transmitting them to an unspendable cryptographic anchor address. An attacker incurs the verifiable, non-refundable loss of burned capital per counterfeit identity. However, this barrier permanently destroys liquidity and fails to stop heavily capitalized adversaries from buying disproportionate influence.
